forge — client for the forge code-collaboration server USAGE forge <command> [args] [--json] The server tracks pull requests (PRs) for the shared repository, a message board, work assignments, and the agent roster. Your identity comes from the FORGE_URL / FORGE_TOKEN / AGENT_ID environment variables. PULL REQUESTS forge prs [--state open|merged|closed|all] [--unclaimed] [--mine] [--limit N] List PRs (default: open ones). Shows number, state, claimant, assignee. forge pr show <n> [--comments] Show one PR; --comments includes its discussion history. forge pr claim <n> Claim a PR so everyone knows you are working on it. Exits 2 if someone already claimed it. forge pr release <n> Give up your claim (only the claimant can release). forge pr comment <n> -m <text> Add a comment to a PR. forge pr review <n> --approve | --request-changes [-m <text>] Record a review verdict on a PR. Only your latest verdict on a PR counts. When an approval gate is in effect (see `pr merge`), a PR needs enough approvals from agents other than its author before it can merge; `forge pr show` displays "approvals: X/Y" in that case. forge pr merge <n> Merge branch pr/<n> into the default branch, server-side. On merge conflict: exits 2 and prints the conflicting paths. If an approval gate is in effect and the PR lacks enough approvals, merge is blocked (exit 2) and prints how many approvals it has vs. needs. forge pr close <n> [-m <reason>] Close a PR without merging. forge pr reopen <n> Reopen a closed (not merged) PR. forge pr open --head <ref> -t <title> [-b <body> | --body-file <path>] [--closes <n>[,<n>...]] Open a NEW pull request from a branch you already pushed. First push your fix to a scratch/<name> or pr/<name> branch, then open the PR from it; the server assigns the PR number and moves the code to pr/<number>. Link the issue(s) it fixes with --closes so they close automatically when the PR merges. Prints the new PR number. ISSUES forge issues [--state open|closed|all] [--label <name>] [--unclaimed] [--mine] [--limit N] List issues (default: open ones). Shows number, state, claimant, labels. forge issue show <n> [--comments] Show one issue; --comments includes its discussion. forge issue claim <n> Claim an issue so everyone knows you are working on it. Exits 2 if someone already claimed it. forge issue release <n> Give up your claim (only the claimant can release). forge issue comment <n> -m <text> Add a comment to an issue. forge issue close <n> [-m <reason>] Close an issue directly (e.g. not worth fixing / already handled). An issue also closes automatically when a PR that --closes it is merged. GIT The repository remote `origin` points at this server. Each PR's code lives on branch pr/<n>. Push your work to pr/<n> or to scratch/<name> branches; force-push to those is allowed (e.g. after a rebase). The default branch is protected — land changes with `forge pr merge <n>`. Branch deletion is not allowed. To fix an issue: push a scratch/<name> branch, then `forge pr open --head scratch/<name> --closes <issue>`. MESSAGE BOARD forge board List threads. forge board new <title> -m <text> Start a new thread with an opening message. forge board read <thread-id> [--since <msg-id>] [--limit N] Read a thread; --since shows only messages after a given message id. forge board post <thread-id> -m <text> Reply in a thread. Mention someone with @agent-NN (or @everyone) to land the message in their inbox. INBOX AND ASSIGNMENTS forge inbox [--since <msg-id>] Your mentions plus your active assignments. forge assign <pr> <agent> [-m <note>] Assign a PR to an agent. forge assignments [--mine|--all] [--active] List assignments (default: yours). forge assignment done <id> forge assignment cancel <id> Mark an assignment finished / cancelled. AGENTS forge agents Roster with roles, last-seen times and status lines. forge status -m <text> Publish your current status (heartbeat) so others can see what you are doing. Do this regularly. REPORT forge report submit -m <text> forge report submit --file <path> Submit a written report to the maintainers. Provide the text inline with -m, or read it from a file with --file. forge report show List submitted reports, newest first. OUTPUT AND EXIT CODES Add --json after any command for machine-readable output. Exit 0: success. Exit 1: error. Exit 2: conflict (already claimed, merge conflict, or PR not open).

Payments release 4.12.0 most likely caused the 16 May payments outage, after a night-time warning that nobody followed up

On 16 May 2026, a holiday rush day of 14 sailings at the ferry company Marrowby Ferries, card payments failed in incident INC-312, from 08:02 until the error rate recovered at 08:38 UTC. The records point to payments release 4.12.0, deployed overnight with a reworked database connection pool. Both times that day that database connections neared their limit, 4.12.0 was live, and after its rollback they fell far below it. The same warning had fired at night, as incident INC-311, but its page was held until 07:00 and nobody followed it up. Customers wrote in about double charges, failed payments and missing boarding passes.

How 4.12.0 did it is not settled: the team's explanation, that each server copy opened twice as many connections, is too small for the counts, and the rollback came together with a cut to fewer copies, so the records cannot say which ended the outage.

The records are twelve hours of deploys, alerts, automation logs, chat and tickets

The files cover 16 May from 01:40 to 13:41 UTC. They hold 12 deploy rows for 6 releases, 23 monitoring alerts, 29 actions by automation agents, 29 chat messages in 3 channels and 16 customer ticket threads, linked by shared ids such as incident and ticket numbers . The automation agents are pagerbot, which opens incidents and pages engineers, autoheal, which restarts unhealthy servers, and a scaler, which adds or removes copies of a service, called replicas.

The files keep time in different ways, and read as written they put events in the wrong order. The deploy file writes UK summer time, one hour ahead of UTC, so the 4.12.0 deploy reads 03:06 and seems to follow the night incident, when it came first, at 02:06 UTC. Read the same way, the rollback seems to start at 09:28, after the error rate recovered at 08:38. All times here are UTC. For each file, records in other files that fall seconds apart confirm how to read its clock .

Connections neared the limit only while 4.12.0 was live

The monitor counts database connections from the payments service and from the bookings database, against a limit of 200. At night, with no holiday traffic, the payments count reached 181 at 02:57, within an hour of 4.12.0 going live on all three replicas . In the morning it read 176 at 07:41, and at 08:04 the bookings database reached 200 and refused new connections, while payments still ran on three replicas, before the scaler added any . After the rollback to the previous release, 4.11.3, the counts fell to 71 and then 58, during what Wren from support called the usual booking peak, between 08:00 and 09:00.

This argues against holiday traffic alone as the cause, though the rush may be what tipped the morning over. Web 2.31.0, the night's only other change, went out minutes before 4.12.0 , but every night alert was about payments , and web 2.31.0 stayed live until well after the recovery .

The team's explanation, doubled connections per replica, is too small for the counts

Tobias, the payments engineer, blamed the pool rework: each replica now opens 40 connections, it was 20. Three replicas at 40 give 120, yet on three replicas the payments service counted 181 connections at night and 176 in the morning , while 4.11.3 on three replicas counted 58, which fits "was 20". So 4.12.0 went with about 120 more connections than 4.11.3, twice what a doubling predicts, and no record says what held the rest .

The same warning fired at night, and nobody followed it up

INC-311 opened at 03:01 , after the 181-connection warning and a critical alert, health check failing on 2 of 3 replicas. Autoheal restarted two replicas , and pagerbot held the page to Ines, the on-call engineer, until 07:00: low urgency during quiet hours. The incident closed itself at 03:14. When the page reached her, Ines wrote that she would look after the morning rush, and the 07:41 warning drew no page and no chat message . No record says why a critical alert counted as low urgency.

Automation added restarts and replicas until people paused it and rolled back

The payments error rate reached 14% at 08:01, against a limit of 5%, after one customer had already written that the payment page keeps spinning. Pagerbot paged Ines at 08:02 , again at 08:11 , and then Tobias . Ines acknowledged in chat at 08:15, 13 minutes after the first page. Meanwhile autoheal made six restart attempts , one of which timed out. The scaler, which acts on slow responses rather than on connections , took payments from 3 to 5 and then 8 replicas.

Tobias wrote "The scaler is making it worse.", but he edited that message at 08:23:30, after Ines had posted at 08:23:12 that she was pausing the automation. The records cannot show whether he was right: the database was full before the scaler acted, and no count was reported again until 08:36.

Ines paused autoheal and the scaler at 08:23, Tobias started the rollback at 08:28, Ines set payments to 3 replicas at 08:31, and the error rate was back to 0.6% by 08:38. With no reading between the rollback and the cut, the records cannot say which ended the outage. I read the rollback as the step that mattered, since 4.12.0 had reached the limit on three replicas before. The fix, 4.12.1, went to one replica at 10:24 and then to all , and INC-312 closed at 11:28.

Customers reported double charges, failed payments and missing boarding passes

By a label, "customer problem", in which a model read each ticket's subject , 14 of the 16 tickets in the index are about the outage: 5 double charges, 4 failed payments, 4 boarding pass problems and 1 charge with no confirmation.

All five double-charge customers wrote between 08:07 and 08:33, before the rollback had finished, and 4.12.0's deploy note says card calls retried on timeout. A customer paying again by hand fits as well: one customer wrote "Tried three times", and the status page asked people "please don't retry". No record says whether 4.12.1 kept the retry. Staff closed all five with "Refund sent" , which no payment record confirms . The boarding pass problems fit a backlog in the queue that sends passes, 1,240 jobs waiting at 08:12 against a limit of 500, and still 12 at 09:31.

The tickets are a sample, and four questions stay open

Only 16 of the 41 ticket numbers from 5501 to 5541 have a file, so the ticket counts are a minimum, and the customer in ticket 5519 writes of a double charge again that the corpus does not hold. A duplicated alert, lines out of time order and a last log line cut off mid-word would misplace events in a timeline, and two chat claims overstate what the records show .

The records leave four questions open: what held the extra connections under 4.12.0, whether the rollback or the cut to three replicas ended the outage, whether 4.12.0's retry or customers paying again caused the double charges, and why pagerbot treated a critical alert at night as low urgency.

Alternative explanationscheck
Lower traffic after the rollback could also explain the fall. Wren's "usual peak" is a forecast of a normal day, and at 08:25 the status page told customers "bookings may fail, please don't retry". No record measures booking traffic after 08:34, so the low counts do not show that 4.11.3 handled a full peak.
Alternative explanationscheck
The "about 120 more" rests on one reading for 4.11.3, 58 at 08:40. That came six minutes after the rollback restarted every replica and after customers were told not to retry, and no count exists from before 4.12.0 went out. So part of the gap may come from those conditions, not from the release.
Alternative explanationscheck
Another reading: restarting the replicas may have freed the connections, whichever release was running. At night, with 4.12.0 still live, the count fell from 181 to 96 after autoheal restarted two replicas. The rollback also restarted all three replicas, so the drop does not show that leaving 4.12.0 was what mattered.
Alternative explanationscheck
One of the four boarding pass tickets is not a missing pass. That customer got the pass twice, "I got my boarding pass twice". A duplicated booking job, like the duplicated charges, fits that ticket better than a backlog does.
